motors.gamma_frame_action: Calibrate this machine's d-axis, then shift gamma by (108 - DAXIS). For its 24s/28p topology the measured DAXIS is 60.0 deg on the 100 mm cross-section, which would make it +48 deg -- not applied, because that is an inference from another machine, not a measurement of this one.

motors.name: 100 mm · 24s/28p mid-torque
motors.description: 100 mm spoke-PM inrunner, 24 slots / 28 poles. 6.0 N·m, 2.39 kW @ 3 800 rpm, 93.1 % eff (FEM) at 46 A, 29.4 V phase-peak — fits the 14-cell (≈50 V) bus. OPTIMIZED: teeth widened 5.0→6.5 mm to relieve saturation + 10 turns of thicker wire → +2.8 pp efficiency vs the first cut, same torque & voltage. F45SH magnets, JFE 20JNEH1200 steel. MTPA γ=+12° (legacy frame: -36°).

protocol.mesh_size_rule: 1.4 mm * D/150, clamped [0.5, 2.0]; solver auto-refines to min(slot,tooth)/2; gap resolved by gap_layers=2 per half-gap

reference_provenance.caveat: The winding source is normalised by the slot's real copper area, so this run was excited at exactly n_wires*I ampere-turns (k = 1). legacy_ampere_turn_scale_k is how far this entry's PREVIOUS reference numbers were off: the old T_avg_maxwell and ripple % over-read by that factor. T_avg is still the energy/flux-linkage mean; what is left between it and T_avg_maxwell is the sliding-band Maxwell residual - see docs/SOLVER_TRIALS_2026-07-30.md, F4+F5 (fixed).
reference_provenance.gamma_frame_caveat: This reference run used gamma = -36 deg read in the CALIBRATED d-axis frame, which is neither the legacy point that number named nor the re-annotated gamma_deg = +12 deg. The reference_* fields are at a different operating point until re-measured (2026-07-31 10:54).
